{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-810t","title":"handle_dao trusts option EUI-64 with no origin or signer binding","description":"File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: security

handle_dao() parses AddressAssignmentRequest::from_dao_bytes() and process() keys the unique-address table on the EUI-64 carried inside option 252. There is no check against a DAO Origin Signature (spec/05-routing.md 8.6), a pinned Announce identity, the IPv6 source IID, or the link-layer signer SIID.

A mesh member that can emit a DAO can ALLOCATE or RELEASE for any other node's EUI-64: occupy their derived/preferred short address, or evict them with RELEASE. process() has no authenticated-identity parameter, so even a caller that verified origin has no API to bind the verified identity to the option EUI.

Client apply_dao_ack() likewise installs assigned_short from the option after only matching the claimed EUI and DAOSequence; it does not require a root-authenticated DAO-ACK.

Canonical vectors are unsigned, so this is the live mutating API as written, not a missing extra feature. Fix: reject assignment DAOs unless the option EUI-64 matches the authenticated origin/signer, and plumb that identity into handle_dao/process. rust/lichen-rpl/src/dao_origin.rs already exists for provenance.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-08-26T17:23:24.440956Z","created_by":"grok","updated_at":"2026-08-26T17:23:24.440956Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-810t","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.1.8.1.2","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-08-26T17:23:24.793903Z","created_by":"grok","metadata":"{}"}]}
